claims.statement: Method reconfiguration or addition without disabling 2FA preserves recovery codes and membership in 2FA-required organizations. This safe migration path differs from disable/re-enable, but describes intended behavior rather than executed continuity proof.

TOTP changes use Settings, Password and authentication, Edit, scan QR or manually enter the setup secret, enter a valid new code and Save. Only after successful save should the existing device method be replaced; secret/QR contents must not enter evidence.

Manual TOTP parameters are TOTP, GitHub:username label, encoded setup secret, issuer GitHub, SHA1, six digits and thirty-second period. These source parameters are not a mandate to weaken other providers, collect real secrets or claim time synchronization verified.

SMS change/addition is FPT/GHEC-only and requires CAPTCHA, country/phone input, sent code and verification, with new CAPTCHA if number changes. Carrier cost, unsupported countries, interception/phishing and deliverability risks qualify the strong preference for TOTP and security-key backups.

Adding more than one authentication and recovery method is recommended, not proof redundancy works. Preferred method selects what appears first at a challenge, not removal of alternatives or phishing resistance. Source addition instructions do not authorize credential changes.

The guide strongly recommends two or more authentication methods plus recovery methods, listing recovery-code file, authentication SSH keys, PATs and verified devices. Backup setup and current recovery-factor availability are distinct; none is verified by file existence alone.

Recovery codes are one-time secrets, downloaded at setup or afterward, and should not be shared/distributed; secure password-manager storage is recommended. Download, Print or Copy are storage choices, not proof of secure custody or permission to collect codes in project evidence.

Generating new recovery codes or disabling/re-enabling 2FA changes codes; editing without disabling does not. Each used code cannot be reused, the listed set has sixteen, and generating a fresh set invalidates every previously generated code; replacement needs approved custody and recovery sequence.

TOTP backup processes vary by provider; links to 1Password, Google and Microsoft are pointers, not imported implementations or executed restore tests. A backup feature is not proof of retained, decryptable, owner-accessible recovery.

The SSH-key recovery pointer specifies authentication key type, not signing-only type. The PAT pointer targets classic tokens and repo scope; this broad capability needs least-privilege review and explicit credential authorization, not automatic token creation or proof all PAT types/scopes recover an account.

The mandatory contributor feature is FPT/GHEC: members of the source-defined required-enrollment cohort cannot disable 2FA and are directed to modify configuration instead. Dated rollout prose does not establish the current target's cohort or grant bypass.

Members, and cloud billing managers, lose repository access where organizations require 2FA if they disable it; the source says re-enabling regains access. Access restoration and role continuity still need independent observation; disablement is not authorized by this review.

Outside collaborators of 2FA-required organizations must first leave or be removed from organization repositories before disabling. This is an access-loss precondition, not permission to remove memberships or transfer ownership.

The Settings, Password and authentication disable menu may require password or another 2FA challenge. Strong recommendation to retain/re-enable 2FA does not authorize temporary weakening or certify safe recovery; no disable operation occurs.

Cloud warning states support cannot restore access when 2FA credentials/recovery methods are lost; exhausted recovery can leave permanent account loss. Email unlinking/reuse is separate from recovering the old account, repositories, permissions or profile.

One-time recovery codes can restore entry through login/social-login cloud alternative, More options, recovery code and Verify. Unknown password may first require reset; an invalid-code error does not justify bypass or invent a success receipt.

An already-added passkey satisfies password and 2FA and can recover without knowing the password. A previously configured security key is described as a secondary authentication method; those capabilities and password prerequisites must not be conflated.

Cloud legacy fallback SMS may still restore access, but new fallback-number configuration is no longer supported; multiple authentication methods are recommended instead. Existing fallback functionality does not authorize enrollment of a removed feature.

Cloud assisted recovery with known password and absent ordinary 2FA/codes can require OTP to primary/backup verified mail, then previously verified device, SSH key or PAT. Prior use does not guarantee availability: factors may be unavailable for security and inactive SSH keys may have been removed.

The guide and resolved review notice say up to/within three business days, while adjacent text describes a 3–5 day waiting period. Preserve this timing discrepancy and do not invent an exact deadline or promise approval; ordinary 2FA/recovery codes can still restore entry during waiting.

The passwordless recovery branch is FPT/GHEC via 2fa-recovery-flow. Reset request uses primary/backup recipients with all verified addresses as backup absent a selected one, and a reset link valid for three hours; passwordless assisted recovery still requires a recovery factor and support review.

Support reviews and emails approval or denial; an approved link must complete recovery, while denial offers support contact. Sending request/email, choosing factor or waiting is not completed recovery. No request, mailbox access, credentials or real support approval is produced.
